newsitem.title: UK: British Biotech lower on Marimastat news.
newsitem.headline: British Biotech lower on Marimastat news.

text.p: Shares in British Biotech Plc rose 4-1/2p to 233-1/2p in pre-trade but quickly retreated to stand 8-1/2p lower at 220-1/2p after the company announced results of clinical trials of its key anti-cancer drug Marimastat.
It said that Phase II trials of Marimastat had confirmed its effectiveness in reducing the rate of rise in cancer antigens and that pivotal clinical Phase III trials were now underway.
However, despite the positive findings, analysts said results of the key Phase III trials were not due until 1998 and that any product launch was unlikely before 1999.

British Biotech's shares have been buoyed by hopes that Marimastat will turn out to be Europe's first big-selling biotech product, with forecasts for annual sales ranging from a few hundred million dollars up to $4.0 billion.
"These are not definitive results. Phase III trials will rigorously test the drug but results are not due until 1998," said one analyst who declined to be named.
"The trials showed there's some effect on antigens but they confirmed there are musculo-skeletar side effects," she added.
Marimastat has been used in trials to treat gastric, colorectal, ovarian and pancreatic cancer.
British Biotech said in a statement that the results of the Phase II trials were encouraging but should be interpreted with caution.
